title: GPU Inference Performance: The Compute Lie Killing Your AI Latency

quotes.text: Lock the provider order, reject CPU fallback, and make the system prove it's fast before it's considered alive. Only then does green mean accelerated.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A concrete, actionable rule for hardening GPU inference deployments.

quotes.text: Silent CPU fallback, version drift and container bloat aren't bugs. They are predictable failure patterns you can block.

chapters.title: The anomaly: idle GPUs, rising latency
Evidence B: CUDA and TensorRT version mismatch

takeaways: If the CUDA or TensorRT execution provider fails to load, ONNX Runtime silently falls back to CPU, so inference services should refuse to start without a verified GPU path.
Pin driver, CUDA, cuDNN, ONNX Runtime and TensorRT versions in one build matrix and prebuild TensorRT engines, because version drift quietly disables fused kernels.
Lean multi-stage container images, explicit GPU device configuration, pinned memory and I/O binding restore predictable P95 latency and throughput.
hook: Paying for GPUs while your AI inference crawls and dashboards stay green? This episode walks engineers and platform teams through three hidden causes: silent CPU fallback, CUDA and TensorRT version drift, and container misconfiguration. You get a hardening checklist that makes acceleration provable instead of assumed.
